subject: Acme Health — DPA questions on TOMs (encryption, key custody) and e-sign workflow
messages:
From: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA TOMs and key custody approach

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. A couple of quick items from our security and procurement teams before we can route to our execs:

- Subprocessors: can you confirm the full subprocessors list and whether any subcontractors will have access to plaintext PHI? We need a definitive list for our vendor review.
- Key custody: Acme Health has a strong preference for customer-controlled keys for any PHI processing. Can Redwood accept a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) integration with a customer KMS (we use AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys)? If not, what mitigations do you offer (e.g., HSM, split-key escrow, zero-access practices)?
- Data transfers: our legal team needs explicit language for EU data transfers — SCCs + appropriate supplementary measures.
- E-sign: can we do a staged e-signature flow? We would like to sign the main DPA first and the TOMs exhibit after we reconcile key management language.

I attached our internal sign-off checklist (referenced in procurement). Please let me know how quickly you can get technical detail and a redline back. We are targeting a late-May start if this moves quickly.

Thanks,
Anna
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA TOMs and key custody approach

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (infrastructure) and Neha (legal/compliance) to propose language and options.

High-level responses now:
- Subprocessors: we'll provide our full subprocessors registry and highlight any with potential access to plaintext.
- Key custody: Redwood supports multiple options depending on the deployment: hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys with HSM protections; for Dedicated/Private we support customer KMS integrations (BYOK) and can accommodate a customer-managed KMS in their VPC. We will outline recommended controls (split-key escrow is not our standard, but we can discuss escrow approaches with legal).
- Transfers: we typically propose SCCs + the EU transfer clause we maintain for our hosted customers; Neha will confirm exact wording.
- E-sign: staged execution is doable. We usually complete the DPA + TOMs together but can accept DPA-first if you need that to meet procurement timelines.

Rishi/Neha — can you provide a short redline and a proposed TOMs exhibit update (encryption/access controls/key mgmt) by EOD tomorrow? Anna, we'll aim to get that to you ASAP.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA TOMs and key custody approach

Hi all — attaching a technical summary and suggested TOMs exhibit edits inline below (see attached PDF: TOMs_exhibit_redline_20270510.pdf). Key points:

1) BYOK / KMS integrations
- For private deployments (VPC/on-prem), we support customer KMS endpoints (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM) via mutual TLS and IAM-based access. Keys remain under customer control; Redwood's inference runtime requests ephemeral data encryption keys (DEKs) that are themselves encrypted by the customer key. That provides zero-knowledge to Redwood operators.
- For hosted customers, we offer a Redwood-managed KMS (HSM-backed) by default. We can offer a hybrid model: customer-managed wrapping key (imported or via external KMS) that wraps Redwood DEKs.

Proposed TOMs language excerpt (short):
- "Encryption & Key Management: Customer Data at rest and in-transit shall be protected using AES-256 or stronger. Cryptographic keys used to encrypt Customer Data will be managed in HSM-backed key stores. For customers electing BYOK, Redwood will support integration with Customer KMS; Redwood will only receive wrapped keys and will not have access to Customer key material in plaintext. Key rotation policies will be implemented per mutually agreed schedule.
- "Zero Access and Operational Controls: Redwood personnel will not have administrative access to Customer key material when BYOK is in use. Audit logs for key usage will be made available to Customer upon request and as part of normal audit evidence"

2) Key escrow and split-key
- We generally avoid third-party escrow because it increases attack surface. If Acme requires escrow, we can add contract language for a two-party escrow arrangement: customer and a mutually agreed escrow provider. Escrow would be treated as an exception and requires separate agreement.

3) Subprocessors
- I'll attach the current subprocessors list (separate registry) and call out those with potential key handling or log-access roles. We recommend adding a clause restricting subprocessors from decrypting data except as strictly necessary for service continuity, and subject to contractually required technical controls.

4) Implementation notes
- For initial rollout: confirm desired mode (Hosted w/ hybrid wrapping key vs Dedicated w/ customer KMS). We can prototype BYOK in a staging environment within 2–3 weeks if procurement signs off.

Anna — happy to do a 30-minute tech call tomorrow if you want to walk through the flow and confirm the integration points (KMS endpoints, TLS certs, IAM roles).

Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: TOMs_exhibit_redline_20270510.pdf, subprocessors_registry_snapshot.csv
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@acmehealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA TOMs and key custody approach

Hi Anna — thanks for the patience. I reviewed Rishi's tech notes and drafted legal redlines for the DPA to reflect BYOK options and stronger TOMs language. High-level legal positions:

- Data transfers: we will incorporate SCCs as the primary transfer mechanism and include a supplementary measures paragraph referencing encryption-at-rest/in-transit and access control mapping. We cannot accept a blanket prohibition on transfers for subprocessors operating in EU regions, but we will commit to notice and objection rights for new subprocessors and an escalation path.
- Key management: the DPA will include an option box — either (a) Customer-managed KMS (preferred for Acme) with the BYOK paragraph that limits Redwood access, or (b) Redwood-managed HSM-backed KMS with specific controls and audit rights.
- Escrow: as Rishi notes, escrow is non-standard. We can offer an escrow playbook as an addendum but would require separate sign-off and security review.
- E-sign: Acme's staged execution request is acceptable. We'll prepare two envelopes if you prefer: one for the DPA now and a second for the TOMs exhibit once the BYOK wording is finalized.

I attached the redlined DPA (Acme_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Please review and let me know if procurement needs any additional concessions on liability caps or data handling specifics. If you confirm BYOK, we will add a short onboarding checklist for KMS connectivity and a timeline for the staging environment.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redline_v3.docx

- Escrow: we will not request escrow at this time.
- Subprocessors: Please send the full subprocessors registry and flag any that will need cross-border access; we'll mark any that require additional scrutiny.
- E-sign: we'll proceed with staged execution. Please send the DocuSign envelope link for the DPA-only envelope. We'll sign that first, then on receipt of the TOMs redline and successful staging test, we'll sign TOMs.
